annotations.text: One hangar, as revised. No head on this screen: the top row is the drawer's x, the build's name as a button, and the points meter. Circles all the way down: solid is equipped, a ring is owned and waiting for a point, a dim grey ring is not yours, and a row with something for sale ends in its price. Pressing a row's word, or anywhere in its dim region, slides the reading in from the right; pips you own still answer a press directly. SAVE stands over the stops only while the kit differs from its name.

The reading is a slide, not a modal: the page moves off left, the panel arrives from the right, and the chevron or a swipe right puts the page back. One panel for every slot: the lesson, the ladder at reading size, and, only where a next rung is for sale, the price, the wallet and BUY. An owned slot is the same panel with the commerce absent.

The name's press slides the builds list in. Two keys and nothing else: NEW slides on to the naming screen, DELETE takes the build the list stands on and dims on the three starters. Picking a row loads it and slides back. Saving is not here: the SAVE key lives at the foot of the ship screen, appearing when the kit has drifted from its name.

NEW's screen, one more slide to the right: a name for the thirty points in hand, and CREATE. Done, it slides back to the list with the new build lit; the chevron or a swipe right abandons it the same way every reading closes.

The budget is a meter and a remainder: what a builder needs mid-edit is how many points are left, not a ratio to decode. Pressing the meter slides in this page, which is where the thirty are explained and the circle grammar is taught. The same slide-in answers every what-is-this on the page, so learning has one gesture.

The first pass, kept as the record. As shipped: five activities in one column, three control grammars, no teaching, and a slot you own none of simply absent, so the page cannot say there is more of this and here is its price. The shelf is smaller than its page suggests: melee sells a new account eight purchases in all, on two stops that both draw the same twenty-three slots.
Fit and buy: one geography, two lenses under a FIT | BUY toggle. It kept the two questions in two moments, and lost to the merge because the price sat a toggle away from the refusal.
Two stops, linked: the smallest change, both tabs kept with a jump between them. It lost because the jump is a context switch mid-build and the two stops keep drawing mostly the same list.
